**Sundhedsklynge Byen** is a healthcare cluster operating within [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] in Denmark [^src5]. It is one of the local organizational units evaluated in the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) annual quality reports, which monitor the treatment and outcomes of patients with [[atrieflimren]] [^src1]. 

The cluster is specifically noted for its performance on Indikator 1, which measures the timeliness of initiating anticoagulation therapy for newly diagnosed patients. In the 2024 reporting period, Sundhedsklynge Byen achieved a result of 88.5%, failing to meet the national standard threshold of 90% [^src1]. 

Beyond initial treatment timeliness, the cluster's clinical practices and patient outcomes are tracked across a wide range of quality indicators. These include 1-year, 2-year, and 5-year anticoagulation treatment coverage rates [^src2], [^src3], as well as adherence to monitoring protocols such as annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOAC therapy [^src4]. The cluster is also evaluated on critical patient outcomes, including the incidence of ischemic stroke and intracranial hemorrhage [^src4], [^src5], the rate of severe bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis [^src6], and the subsequent development of heart failure [^src6], [^src7]. Furthermore, Sundhedsklynge Byen is included in national geographic mapping of stroke incidence ([[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]) to visualize regional variations in care quality [^src4]. 

Ultimately, the data collected on Sundhedsklynge Byen serves as a benchmarking tool within Denmark's hierarchical quality improvement strategy, enabling local and regional health authorities to identify strengths and vulnerabilities in their cardiovascular care and stroke prevention efforts.
